arxiv-1611-02297.title: Dynamical modeling validation of parent bodies associated with newly discovered CMN meteor showers
arxiv-1611-02297.creator: Damir Šegon, Jérémie Vaubaillon, Peter S. Gural, Denis Vida, Željko Andreić, Korado Korlević, Ivica Skokić
arxiv-1611-02297.description: Abstract Context. Results from previous searches for new meteor showers in the combined Croatian Meteor Network and SonotaCo meteor databases suggested possible parent bodies for several newly identified showers. Aims. We aim to perform an analysis to validate the connection between the identified showers and candidate parent bodies. Methods.

arxiv-2112-14927.title: An Empirical Study of Security Practices for Microservices Systems
arxiv-2112-14927.creator: Rezaei Nasab Ali, Shahin Mojtaba, Hoseyni Raviz Seyed Ali, Liang Peng, Mashmool Amir, Lenarduzzi Valentina
arxiv-2112-14927.description: Abstract Despite the numerous benefits of microservices systems, security has been a critical issue in such systems. Several factors explain this difficulty, including a knowledge gap among microservices practitioners on properly securing a microservices system. To (partially) bridge this gap, we conducted an empirical study.

arxiv-2212-02408.title: A low-rank algorithm for evaluating Lyapunov operator φ \varphi -functions within matrix-valued exponential integrators
arxiv-2212-02408.creator: Dongping Li, Xiuying Zhang, Hongjiong Tian
arxiv-2212-02408.description: Abstract In this work we present a low-rank algorithm for computing low-rank approximations of large-scale Lyapunov operator φ \varphi -functions. These computations play a crucial role in implementing of matrix-valued exponential integrators for large-scale stiff matrix differential equations, where the (approximate) solutions are of low rank.

arxiv-2306-04523.title: Can current NLI systems handle German word order? Investigating language model performance on a new German challenge set of minimal pairs
arxiv-2306-04523.creator: Ines Reinig, Katja Markert
arxiv-2306-04523.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ines Reinig, Katja Markert. Compared to English, German word order is freer and therefore poses additional challenges for natural language inference (NLI). We create WOGLI (Word Order in German Language Inference), the first adversarial NLI dataset for German word order that has the following properties: (i) each premise has an entailed and a non-entailed hypothesis; (ii) premise and hypotheses differ only in word order and necessary morphological changes to mark case and number.

arxiv-2412-01757.title: Structure-Guided Input Graph for GNNs facing Heterophily Thanks: This work was partially supported by NSF under award CCF-2340481, Spanish AEI Grants FPU20-05554, PID2022-136887NB-I00 and by the Autonomous Community of Madrid (course of action num. 3, Excellence Program within the multi-year agreeme
arxiv-2412-01757.creator: Victor M. Tenorio, Madeline Navarro, Samuel Rey, Santiago Segarra, and Antonio G. Marques
arxiv-2412-01757.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Victor M. Tenorio, Madeline Navarro, Samuel Rey, Santiago Segarra, and Antonio G. Marques. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a promising tool to handle data exhibiting an irregular structure. However, most GNN architectures perform well on homophilic datasets, where the labels of neighboring nodes are likely to be the same. In recent years, an increasing body of work has been devoted to the development of GNN architectures for heterophilic datasets, where labels do not exhibit this low-pass behavior.

arxiv-2512-13287.title: Tidally Perturbed, Rotating Stellar Systems: Asynchronous Equilibria 2022 Tidally Perturbed, Rotating Stellar Systems: Asynchronous Equilibria – B
arxiv-2512-13287.creator: Lucy A. Z. Arditi, Anna Lisa Varri
arxiv-2512-13287.description: Abstract We present a new three-parameter family of self-consistent equilibrium models for quasi-relaxed stellar systems that are subject to the combined action of external tides and rigid internal rotation. These models provide an idealised description of globular clusters that rotate asynchronously with respect to their orbital motion around a host galaxy.

pmc-10623857.title: Revealing the developmental characterization of rumen microbiome and its host in newly received cattle during receiving period contributes to formulating precise nutritional strategies
pmc-10623857.creator: Yanjiao Li, Kang Mao, Yitian Zang, Guwei Lu, Qinghua Qiu, Kehui Ouyang, Xianghui Zhao, Xiaozhen Song, Lanjiao Xu, Huan Liang, Mingren Qu
pmc-10623857.description: BackgroundMinimizing mortality losses due to multiple stress and obtaining maximum performance are the production goals for newly received cattle. In recent years, vaccination and metaphylaxis treatment significantly decreased the mortality rate of newly received cattle, while the growth block induced by treatment is still obvious. Assessment of blood metabolites and behavior monitoring offer potential for early identification of morbid animals.

pmc-11409065.title: GeneSPIDER2: large scale GRN simulation and benchmarking with perturbed single-cell data
pmc-11409065.creator: Mateusz Garbulowski, Thomas Hillerton, Daniel Morgan, Deniz Seçilmiş, Lisbet Sonnhammer, Andreas Tjärnberg, Torbjörn E M Nordling, Erik L L Sonnhammer
pmc-11409065.description: Single-cell data is increasingly used for gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, and benchmarks for this have been developed based on simulated data. However, existing single-cell simulators cannot model the effects of gene perturbations. A further challenge lies in generating large-scale GRNs that often struggle with computational and stability issues.

pmc-11494580.title: Prognostic impact based on tumor diameter of pathological N1 lymph node metastases for non-small cell lung cancer
pmc-11494580.creator: Yasuko Kurose, Yoko Azuma, Akira Iyoda, Naobumi Tochigi
pmc-11494580.description: BackgroundThe N parameter in the tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) classification of lung cancer is categorized according to the location of nodal metastasis, while that for some other cancers are classified according to the size and number of metastatic foci. In lung cancer, the impact of size of nodal metastasis on prognosis is unclear.

pmc-11674294.title: Evaluation of Thermal Liquid Biopsy Analysis of Saliva and Blood Plasma Specimens as a Novel Diagnostic Modality in Head and Neck Cancer
pmc-11674294.creator: Gabriela Schneider, Alagammai Kaliappan, Nathan Joos, Laura M Dooley, Brian S Shumway, Jonathan B Chaires, Wolfgang Zacharias, Jeffrey M Bumpous, Nichola C Garbett, Juan P Rodrigo
pmc-11674294.description: Simple SummaryIn recent years, researchers have been investigating saliva as a potential tool for the early detection of cancer and to monitor patients’ health. Saliva is easy to collect, making it a good alternative to blood tests. This study evaluated a research technique called thermal liquid biopsy (TLB) to analyze saliva from patients with head and neck cancer (HNC).

pmc-12766770.title: Incidence of diaphragmatic dysfunction after non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: a prospective, single-centre observational study protocol
pmc-12766770.creator: Karim Guessous, Yoann Elmaleh, Fehmi Kattou, Matthieu Coblence, Pierre Dore, Nabil Zanoun
pmc-12766770.description: IntroductionPersisting diaphragmatic dysfunction (DD) for more than 24 hours after thoracic surgery is associated with higher rates of pulmonary complications and prolonged intensive care unit stays. Despite advances in less invasive techniques, the incidence of DD remains significant, affecting ~55%–68% of patients after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS).
